headline: The best validated 80 x 80 inverse-designed bend (adjoint seed 5, shared 20 x 20 representation) meets the release gates on the training spectrum, the 61-wavelength held-out spectrum and the half-cell grid (worst case over eroded, nominal and dilated masks: IL 0.1718 dB, RL 22.99 dB held-out; gates IL < 0.50 dB, RL >= 22 dB), and beats the best tested conventional bend (bezier:0.45, robust IL 0.3306 dB) by 0.1595 / 0.1588 / 0.1611 dB (training / 61 held-out / half-cell grid), more than the largest measured grid change (0.0026 dB). The full-resolution phase 1 run (phase1 r_f 6; bend80_phase1.gds, kept as the record of the unconstrained-grid failure mode) meets the release gates on the training spectrum, the 61-wavelength held-out spectrum and the half-cell grid (worst case over eroded, nominal and dilated masks: IL 0.2737 dB, RL 22.31 dB held-out; gates IL < 0.50 dB, RL >= 22 dB), but does not beat the best tested conventional bend (bezier:0.45, robust IL 0.3306 dB) by the required 0.10 dB: the gain is 0.0569 / 0.0569 / 0.0575 dB. The release design was chosen by the lowest training-set robust J among the designs that meet every gate; the protocol did not name it in advance, and the choice does not use held-out data.
failures: Phase 1: 23 of 25 scored masks of the r_f 6 run failed the geometry gates; the chosen design is the scored mask of it 3, of 96 iterations. The final relaxed iterate (post-hoc diagnostic, not a candidate) reaches a robust IL of 0.0877 dB and RL 24.41 dB held-out, but its nominal mask has 1 floating silicon component, 8 width and 11 gap violations (minimum width 2 cells, minimum gap 3 cells): the projection-based length-scale control did not hold. Earlier, a nominal-only 80 x 80 run (Stage 5 stretch, 0.0376 dB) also failed the 5-cell width rule; it is not a release target. Release design (adjoint seed 5): the nominal mask meets every geometry rule, but the biased masks do not: eroded layer 4 width and 0 gap violations, dilated layer 2 width and 2 gap violations (reported, not gated).
unverified: RTL: the SystemVerilog stencil is bit-exact with its software reference in Verilator on two test cases only; no synthesis figures. No Lean proof in this release candidate. The layout scale is illustrative. The independent layout reader is a second implementation by the same author, not a commercial DRC tool.
benchmark_verdict: Benchmark (5 seeds per method, cap 1200 charged solves): discrete adjoint: median best J 0.2166 dB (range 0.1711 to 0.2949), T1 in 5/5 runs, T2 in 3/5 runs; CMA-ES: median best J 2.0659 dB (range 0.8128 to 3.9520), T1 in 0/5 runs, T2 in 0/5 runs; one-step PPO: median best J 0.3766 dB (range 0.3261 to 0.5371), T1 in 4/5 runs, T2 in 0/5 runs. discrete adjoint vs CMA-ES: discrete adjoint leads (the ranges of best J at the cap do not overlap); discrete adjoint vs one-step PPO: inconclusive (one-step PPO stopped below 90 % of the cap in at least one run); CMA-ES vs one-step PPO: inconclusive (one-step PPO stopped below 90 % of the cap in at least one run). one-step PPO runs ended at the 20000-candidate stop rule of stage6_bb, because most samples failed the geometry gates (free to score); that rule is in the committed binary but not in the protocol.
negative_results: CMA-ES never reaches T2 (J <= best baseline - 0.10 dB) in any run; one-step PPO never reaches T2 (J <= best baseline - 0.10 dB) in any run.
